newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's forex market closed for holiday. [CORRECTED 07:38 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Israel's forex market closed for holiday. [CORRECTED 07:38 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects earlier story by adding that Israel's commercial banks are dealing in foreign currency on Monday. Only the central Bank of Israel is closed and therefore no representative rate for the shekel will be set.)

The central Bank of Israel is closed on Monday due to the Jewish holiday of Shushan Purim, celebrated in Jerusalem, and therefore no representative rate for the shekel will be set. Commercial banks, however, are dealing in foreign currency.
The Bank of Israel will reopen on Tuesday.
The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange will reopen on Monday after being closed on Sunday.
